items.title: REPORT: HCL's $18 Million CEO Package Reflects Bet on India's AI Infrastructure Future
items.summary:
HCL Tech's C Vijay Kumar just became India's highest-paid IT services CEO with a ₹174.86 crore package for fiscal year 26, a 67% jump from last year. That's $18.13 million built from base salary, performance bonuses, cash LTI, and RSU payouts that did most of the heavy lifting. For context, he now earns more than the chiefs of TCS, Infosys, and Wipro combined for two years straight.

The board pre-approved this trajectory, so it wasn't a surprise move. But the timing is sharp. HCL just committed ₹3,500 crore to an AI data center business and posted its highest-ever Q1 bookings. Vijay Kumar frames his bet on five vectors: service transformation, differentiated IP, AI growth opportunities, ecosystem partnerships, and upskilling. While the rest of Indian IT wrestles with margin pressure and cautious guidance, HCL's leadership is doubling down on infrastructure as its competitive advantage in the AI era.

items.title: Building time crystals with quantum computers
items.summary:
Crystals are defined by repeating patterns—but what if those patterns unfold in time rather than space? In this episode of The Coherence Times, we take a closer look at “time crystals”—systems of interacting particles that exhibit unique behaviors when driven by regular pulses of energy.

Join host Ryan Mandelbaum as they speak with Dr. Eric Switzer and Dr. Nicolás Lorente, two researchers who recently used IBM’s quantum computers to create and study a two-dimensional time crystal. Together, they break down what it means for a system to behave like a crystal in time, why studying systems out of equilibrium matters, and how quantum computers enable experiments that go beyond the limitations of purely classical methods.

items.title: ALERT: Seoul Semiconductor's India Plant Could Be Built in Months, Not Years
items.summary:
Five days after Semicon 2.0 was approved with ₹1,27,500 crore backing, Seoul Semiconductor confirmed it's assessing a manufacturing plant in India. The Korean LED and opto-electronics giant just triggered a three-state bidding war between Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Gujarat. This is Seoul's first India production base ever. It currently manufactures only in South Korea, the US, China, and Vietnam.

Here's what matters: this isn't a chip fab. It's an assembly and packaging unit, which needs far less capital, water, and construction time. If greenlit, it could go from board approval to production in months, not years. Seoul ranks 3rd globally in LED semiconductors, holds 18,000+ patents, and was the only top-three player to hold both revenue and market share through the 2024 LED downturn. Korean chip suppliers are officially diversifying away from China concentration toward India's growing electronics market, and this deal signals they mean business.

items.title: ALERT: Paytm's Board Rejected Bonus Shares Even With ₹222 Crore Quarterly Profit
items.summary:
Paytm's board made a counterintuitive call after delivering blockbuster Q1 results. With consolidated net profit up 78.8% year-on-year to ₹222 crore and operating revenue growing 27.6% to ₹2,448 crore, investors expected a bonus share announcement. Instead, the board rejected it. The board's reasoning was direct: in a company that only recently turned consistently profitable, capital discipline matters more than a stock price sugar rush.

The company approved an additional ₹100 crore investment in wholly-owned subsidiary Paytm Money to fuel technology and regulatory capital needs. It also asked shareholders to extend the deadline for deploying leftover IPO funds to March 2029, reallocating capital toward core payments and strengthening the finserve ecosystem. In a leadership update, Google Search's former SVP Amitabh Kumar Singh joined as a non-executive director.
